ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a three-dimensional silicon n-channel MOS transistor, with the gate labeled G at the top; the oxide layer thickness below the gate is labeled 1 nm; the source region S is on the right side, and the drain region D is on the left side. In the figure, at the gate edge of the source terminal, a small gate-source overlap strip with length δ is marked, and the device width direction is labeled 1 μm. Therefore, the required gate-source overlap capacitance corresponds to a parallel-plate capacitor on the source-terminal side with length δ, width 1 μm, and dielectric of 1 nm SiO2. Reasoning: Take δ = 20 nm, width W = 1 μm, oxide layer thickness tox = 1 nm, εox = 3.9ε0 = 3.9 × 8.9 × 10^-12 F/m. The overlap area A = δW = (20 × 10^-9)(1 × 10^-6) m^2. The capacitance Cgs,ov = εox A / tox = (3.9)(8.9 × 10^-12)(20 × 10^-9)(1 × 10^-6)/(1 × 10^-9) F = 6.94 × 10^-16 F = 0.694 fF, approximately 0.7 fF.
